title: Chicken or Turkey Salad with Light Creamy Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey salad with a light creamy dressing combines tender poultry, fresh vegetables, and a smooth sauce made from yogurt or light mayonnaise. It works as a light lunch or a side dish for dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are excellent sources of lean protein that digest easily.
A light creamy dressing is often made with low‑fat yogurt, reducing calories compared with traditional mayo.
The salad can be prepared quickly: cook or grill the meat, chop the veggies, and toss with the dressing.
Variations of the dressing may include mustard, lemon juice, herbs, and spices for flavor diversity.
It is a popular summer dish because it is refreshing and not heavy.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Poultry provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Using a yogurt‑based dressing dramatically cuts saturated fat content.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and turkey supply B6 and B12, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from vegetables
items.content: Fresh vegetables such as tomatoes, cucumbers, and peppers add dietary fiber for healthy digestion.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: The dish does not cause rapid blood‑sugar spikes, making it suitable for weight management.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to chicken or turkey.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared dressings can contain salt; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portions.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked or improperly stored poultry can harbor salmonella; ensure thorough cooking and refrigeration.

items.title: Lactose in dressing
items.content: If the dressing uses yogurt, those with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, optionally with whole‑grain bread or crackers. It is convenient in a lunch container or as a side to a main course.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. If the dressing is stored separately, it stays fresh longer.
